questiontext.text:
\(\mathbf{a} = {@cv3(A)@}\). For each vector, choose whether it is parallel to \(\mathbf{a}\) in the same direction, parallel in the opposite direction, or not parallel.

\({@cv3(v1)@}\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
\({@cv3(v2)@}\): [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
\({@cv3(v3)@}\): [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
\({@cv3(v4)@}\): [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
One vector is parallel to another when it is a number times the other, the same number for every component. Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\).

  • \({@cv3(v1)@}\): the ratios are \({@rt1[1]@}\), \({@rt1[2]@}\), \({@rt1[3]@}\). [[if test="nt1"]]They are not all equal, so it is not parallel to \(\mathbf{a}\).[[else]]Each is \({@k1@}\), so the vector is \([[if test="is(k1 = 1)"]][[else]][[if test="is(k1 = -1)"]]-[[else]]{@k1@}[[/if]][[/if]]\mathbf{a}\): parallel, [[if test="sm1"]]same direction.[[else]]opposite direction.[[/if]][[/if]]
  • \({@cv3(v2)@}\): the ratios are \({@rt2[1]@}\), \({@rt2[2]@}\), \({@rt2[3]@}\). [[if test="nt4"]]They are not all equal, so it is not parallel to \(\mathbf{a}\).[[else]]Each is \({@k4@}\), so the vector is \([[if test="is(k4 = 1)"]][[else]][[if test="is(k4 = -1)"]]-[[else]]{@k4@}[[/if]][[/if]]\mathbf{a}\): parallel, [[if test="sm4"]]same direction.[[else]]opposite direction.[[/if]][[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Vectors II: parallel, opposite or not parallel

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.6: Decide whether each of four three-dimensional vectors is parallel to a given vector, and in which direction.

Core

This question is adapted from Question 4 in Exercise C and Question C5 in Section C of Chapter 9 of Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Core 4 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2005: sorting turned into a classification with direction, new vectors with near misses, randomised over a curated list, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

node.description: Direction swapped, or near miss taken as parallel

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="pr1"]]

It is parallel to \(\mathbf{a}\), but check the direction. The same direction needs a positive multiplier and the opposite direction a negative one: the top components give \({@v1[1]@} \div ({@A[1]@}) = {@rt1[1]@}\).

[[else]]

You chose parallel, which needs the same multiplier for every component. Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): the top components give \({@v1[1]@} \div ({@A[1]@}) = {@rt1[1]@}\). Work out the other two and compare.

[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="pr1"]]

You chose not parallel, which means the three multipliers are not all equal. Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): the top components give \({@v1[1]@} \div ({@A[1]@}) = {@rt1[1]@}\). Work out the other two and compare.

[[else]]

You chose parallel, which needs the same multiplier for every component. Divide each component by the matching component of \(\mathbf{a}\): the top components give \({@v1[1]@} \div ({@A[1]@}) = {@rt1[1]@}\). Work out the other two and compare.

[[/if]]
